Hitzewelle: Hitze breitet sich im Süden aus – Fast 33 Grad in Südbaden

Körperbild: Der Körper muss ein Komplize sein
zeit.description: Kinder lernen früh, ihren Körper zu bewerten. Auch, weil Eltern es so vorleben. Wer ein gesundes Körperbild vermitteln will, muss auf vier Ebenen von Einflüssen achten.

zeit.title: Fed: US-Notenbank lässt Leitzins unverändert
zeit.description: Der neue Fed-Chef Kevin Warsh hat Donald Trumps Forderungen nach einer Zinssenkung nicht umgesetzt. Die Spanne für den Leitzins bleibt bei 3,5 bis 3,75 Prozent.

zeit.title: Schwarz-rote Koalition: SPD wirft Bildungsministerin Prien schlechte Zusammenarbeit vor
zeit.description: Bildungsministerin Prien will das Förderprogramm »Demokratie leben!« umbauen. SPD-Abgeordnete werfen ihr in einem Brief vor, bei der Planung übergangen worden zu sein.

zeit.title: Smartphoneverbot in Afghanistan: Taliban verhängen Smartphoneverbot für Regierungsmitarbeiter
zeit.description: Afghanische Regierungsbeamte dürfen nach einer Anordnung der Taliban ihre Smartphones nicht mehr nutzen. Verstöße sollen bestraft werden – jedoch ist unklar, wie.

zeit.title: Kennzeichnungspflicht von Gentechnik: Gut für die Konzerne, schlecht für Verbraucher und die Umwelt
zeit.description: Kaum Auflagen, wenig Kontrollen: Die EU ist Wissenschaftsmarketing erlegen und lockert die Regeln für Gentechnik. Damit schützt sie vor allem Geschäftsinteressen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Fussball-WM 2026: Portugal kommt gegen Aussenseiter Kongo-Kinshasa nicht über das 1:1 hinaus +++ Muheim verpasst Spiel gegen Bosnien-Herzegowina
nzz.description: Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten zur Fussball-WM in Kanada, Mexiko und den USA.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Polizei-News aus Zürich: Velofahrer bei Kollision mit Bus in Birmensdorf tödlich verletzt +++ Anklage wegen Betrugsfall mit Daten von Arbeitslosen
nzz.description: Die neuesten Polizeimeldungen aus der Region.

nzz.title: Krachende Niederlage für Bundesrat Parmelin: Der Nationalrat erteilt dem Mercosur-Abkommen eine Abfuhr
nzz.description: Obwohl die Bedeutung für die Industrie unbestritten ist, scheitert das Freihandelsabkommen mit vier südamerikanischen Staaten an einer unheiligen Allianz von SVP, SP und Grünen.

nzz.title: Auch Kevin Warsh lässt Trump warten: Das Fed belässt den Leitzins unverändert
nzz.description: Die hohe Inflation und der starke Arbeitsmarkt in den USA lassen Zinssenkungen in weite Ferne rücken. Die Prognosen der Zentralbanker lassen sogar den Schluss zu, dass 2026 noch eine Zinserhöhung anstehen könnte.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Staatschefs, Tränengas und ein brennendes Auto: die Bilder des G-7-Gipfels – und der Anti-G-7-Demonstration in Genf
nzz.description: Vom 15. bis 17. Juni findet in Évian auf der französischen Seite des Genfersees der G-7-Gipfel statt. In Genf ist am Sonntag gegen die Veranstaltung demonstriert worden, teilweise mit Gewalt.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - G-7-Gipfel in Évian: Trump nähert sich G-7-Partnern an +++ Obergrenze für Rohstoffimporte aus China geplant
nzz.description: Von Montag bis Mittwoch empfängt Emmanuel Macron in Évian am Genfersee die Staats- und Regierungschefs der G-7. Frankreich und die Schweiz haben sich mit einem grossen Sicherheitsdispositiv auf Proteste vorbereitet. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Ticker.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Trump stellt Unterschrift auf dem Bürgenstock bereits ab Donnerstag in Aussicht +++ Pezeshkian bezeichnet das Rahmenabkommen als einen diplomatischen Sieg für Iran
nzz.description: Seit April gilt eine Waffenruhe zwischen den USA, Israel und Iran. Doch in den vergangenen Tagen griffen sich die Staaten gegenseitig an. Die Folgen des Konflikts sind weltweit spürbar. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Live-Ticker.

nzz.title: Reaktion auf Mafia-Fall und Brandkatastrophe von Crans-Montana: Kantone sollen systematisch Strafregisterauszüge von EU-Bürgern einfordern
nzz.description: Das Parlament zieht Konsequenzen: Für vorbestrafte EU- und Efta-Bürger soll es keine Aufenthaltsbewilligungen mehr geben. Die Vorgabe steht in direktem Widerspruch zur Personenfreizügigkeit.

nzz.title: Für die Schweiz geht es an der WM früh um viel – vor dem Spiel gegen Bosnien-Herzegowina herrscht Spannung, auch wegen Granit Xhaka
nzz.description: Die letzten Tage haben Zweifel am Zustand der Schweizer Nationalmannschaft geschürt. Ein Sieg am Donnerstag würde ihr das Leben erleichtern.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Ein Gipfel, um Trump zu bespassen
nzz.description: Die G-7 tut noch immer so, als wäre sie ein politisches Direktorium der Weltgemeinschaft. Das ist sie aber schon lange nicht mehr.

nzz.title: Mit Drohnen, Tauchern und Delfinen: Die Amerikaner wollen die Strasse von Hormuz so schnell wie möglich öffnen
nzz.description: Der für die Weltwirtschaft so wichtige Wasserweg sei ab sofort wieder frei, verkündete Präsident Trump am Sonntag. Doch dazu muss er erst einmal von Minen geräumt werden. Die meisten grossen Reedereien warten vorerst lieber ab.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Die Koalition will die Tabak- und Alkoholsteuer erhöhen: Damit werden die wirklichen Probleme im Gesundheitswesen nur verschleiert
nzz.description: Koalitionspolitiker verkaufen die Steuererhöhungen als Prävention. Doch das ist scheinheilig. An echten Reformen führt kein Weg vorbei.

nzz.title: Die SRG verzichtet auf die Champions League: Keine Spiele der Königsklasse mehr
nzz.description: Der prestigeträchtigste Wettbewerb im europäischen Klubfussball wird nur noch diese Saison auf den Sendern der SRG zu sehen sein. Für die neuen Rechte wird der öffentlich-rechtliche Rundfunk nicht mehr mitbieten.

nzz.title: Rechner statt Motorensound: Der neue Mercedes GLC EQ wird zum rollenden Datengerät
nzz.description: Vier Supercomputer, KI-gestützte Assistenten, permanente Cloud-Anbindung und Over-the-Air-Updates machen das E-SUV zum ersten konsequent softwarebasierten Mercedes und verschieben den Schwerpunkt vom Antrieb zur digitalen Plattform.

nzz.title: China-Markt im freien Fall: So verschärft sich die Krise der deutschen Autohersteller
nzz.description: Der Absatz von Neuwagen bricht ein, mit BMW ist auch der bisherige Musterschüler hart davon betroffen. Die einstige Wachstumsregion wird zum unkalkulierbaren Risiko.

nzz.title: Der mutmassliche Millionenbetrüger Ali Syed kommt frei – die Schuldfrage ist noch offen
nzz.description: Das Bundesgericht rügt die Zürcher Justiz. Wegen Verfahrensfehlern wird der gebürtige Inder aus der Haft entlassen.

france24fr.title: Ce que contient l'accord négocié entre l'Iran et les États-Unis
france24fr.description: Les États-Unis ont dévoilé mercredi le texte du protocole d'accord conclu avec l'Iran, avant la signature officielle du document prévue vendredi. Dans ces quatorze points, Téhéran s'engage notamment à diluer ses stocks d'uranium enrichi dans le cadre de négociations à mener sous 60 jours. En contrepartie, les États-Unis prévoient une levée progressive des sanctions.

france24fr.title: Angleterre - Croatie en direct : suivez le remake de la demi-finale de la Coupe du monde 2018
france24fr.description: L'Angleterre d'Harry Kane affronte la Croatie de Luka Modric dans le groupe L de la Coupe du monde. Qui des Three Lions ou des Vatreni va l'emporter ? Suivez le match en direct grâce à notre live commenté.

france24fr.title: Coupe du monde : la RD Congo écrit son histoire en tenant en échec le Portugal et Ronaldo
Coupe du monde : la RD Congo écrit son histoire en tenant en échec le Portugal et Ronaldo
france24fr.description: La RD Congo a soigné son retour à la Coupe du monde. Les Léopards de Chancel Mbemba ont muselé le Portugal de Cristiano Ronaldo et arraché un point du match nul (1-1), précieux dans la course vers les 16es de finale.

france24fr.title: Trump et Macron à Versailles : un dîner pour quoi faire ?
france24fr.description: Emmanuel Macron s'apprête à recevoir Donald Trump au château de Versailles mercredi soir. Il est attendu par le chef de l'État français et son épouse pour une visite de la Galerie des Glaces puis un concert dans la chapelle royale, avant un dîner servi dans la Galerie basse, en présence des ministres français et américains des Affaires étrangères et de l'Économie et d'une trentaine d'invités. Quel est l'objectif d'une telle soirée ? Précisions de James André, journaliste France 24 à Versailles,

france24fr.title: Donald Trump assure que l'accord avec l'Iran sera "bientôt" signé
france24fr.description: Le président américain a indiqué, lors de sa conférence de presse à la clôture du sommet du G7 à Évian-les-Bains, que le protocole d'accord avec l'Iran pour mettre fin à la guerre au Moyen-Orient serait signé "bientôt". Il a également vanté son "formidable partenariat" avec le Premier ministre israélien Benjamin Netanyahu, un changement de ton après ses critiques acerbes de la veille. Analyse d'Antoine Mariotti, chroniqueur international France 24.

france24fr.title: La bulle IA va-t-elle éclater ?
france24fr.description: Au G7 d’Évian, les géants de la tech comme Sam Altman (OpenAI), Dario Amodei (Anthropic) ou Arthur Mensch (Mistral AI) ont été conviés pour parler d’intelligence artificielle. Des patrons devenus aussi importants que des chefs d’État. Mais l’enjeu n’est pas seulement économique, il est aussi démocratique. La décision de Donald Trump de restreindre l’accès aux derniers modèles d’Anthropic souligne la dépendance de l’Europe aux États-Unis, sur fond de bras de fer autour de la régulation de l’IA.

france24fr.title: Donald Trump défend l'accord de cessez-le-feu avec l'Iran au sommet du G7
france24fr.description: Donald Trump s'est exprimé à l'issu du sommet du G7 qui se tenait à Évian-les-Bains, un des "meilleurs G7 de l'histoire" selon le président américain. Regardez sa prise de parole en replay sur France 24.

france24fr.title: Portugal - RD Congo : revivez l'exploit historique des Léopards
france24fr.description: Le Portugal de Cristiano Ronaldo affrontait la RD Congo de Chancel Mbemba mercredi à Houston pour le premier match du groupe K de la Coupe du monde. Revivez le match nul historique arraché par les Léopards  grâce au direct commenté animé par nos confrères de RFI.

france24fr.title: Guerre au Moyen-Orient : un accord qui vaut des milliards de dollars pour Téhéran
france24fr.description: Le détail du protocole d’entente signé par les États-Unis et l’Iran a été dévoilé par plusieurs médias. À quelques jours de la signature officielle de ce document qui doit servir de feuille de route pour les négociations de paix, ce texte semble aller dans le sens de l’Iran. Surtout d’un point de vue financier. Et au détriment du peuple iranien ?

france24fr.title: IA, Iran, Ukraine : Emmanuel Macron fait le bilan du G7
france24fr.description: Le président français Emmanuel Macron s'est félicité ce mercredi d'un "succès" et d'un "moment d'unité" au sommet du G7 qui s'est tenu à Évian-les-Bains, après des mois de "désaccords". Regardez sa prise de parole en replay.

france24fr.title: Cisjordanie occupée : deux mosquées incendiées par des colons israéliens
france24fr.description: Dans la nuit, deux mosquées ont été visées par des attaques attribuées à des colons israéliens.Les lieux de culte palestiniens sont devenus des cibles récurrentes d’attaques menées par des colons israéliens, alors que la présence de ceux-ci continue de s’étendre en Cisjordanie occupée. À l’extérieur des bâtiments, des graffitis en hébreu portant le mot "vengeance" ont été retrouvés sur les murs. france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la Croatie espère jouer un nouveau tour à l’Angleterre
france24fr.description: Le groupe L de la Coupe du monde s’ouvre avec une affiche alléchante : Angleterre - Croatie. Les deux sélections s’étaient affrontées lors de la demi-finale du Mondial 2018, qui s’était soldée par une victoire des coéquipiers de Luka Modric en prolongation. Les Three Lions auront à cœur de faire oublier ce douloureux souvenir à leurs supporters.

france24fr.title: Russie, IA, "confiance" en Trump... Ce qu'il faut retenir du discours de Macron en clôture du G7
france24fr.description: Lors d'une conférence de presse de clôture mercredi, au dernier jour du sommet du G7 organisé en France, Emmanuel Macron a notamment évoqué une "remobilisation" du Groupe des sept "extrêmement importante" pour accroître la pression sur la Russie. Il a également appelé à "mieux réguler" l'intelligence artificielle et assuré "avoir toujours eu" confiance dans le président américain Donald Trump.

france24fr.title: Cameroun : l'opposant Tchiroma porte plainte contre Paul Biya en France
france24fr.description: Issa Tchiroma Bakary, candidat malheureux à la présidentielle camerounaise de 2025, a déposé deux plaintes pénales auprès du tribunal judiciaire de Paris contre le président Paul Biya. Exilé en Gambie, il conteste la réélection de Paul Biya et dénonce la répression dont il a été victime avec ses partisans. Précisions de Marcel Amoko, correspondant de France 24 à Yaoundé.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : les journalistes sénégalais craignent de ne pas pouvoir suivre les Lions
france24fr.description: Les restrictions de visa aux États-Unis empêchent la presse sportive sénégalaise de couvrir tous les matches des Lions de la Teranga car ils devront se déplacer au Canada. Or, avec une seule entrée autorisée, les journalistes ne pourront pas retourner sur le territoire américain après ce déplacement international. Une situation "désolante", selon le journaliste sénégalais Grégoire Samba Ngom.

france24fr.title: 50 ans plus tard, l'Afrique du Sud se rappelle les émeutes de Soweto
france24fr.description: C’est dans un contexte de violences contre les étranger que les victimes  des émeutes de Soweto, le 16 juin 1976 luttent contre l'oubli. À l'époque, des étudiants noirs ont été réprimés par la police de Johannesburg dans un terrible massacre. Au moins 176 personnes sont mortes sous leurs balles. Récit de Lou Kisiela.

france24fr.title: Marseillaise remplacée, défilé d’une "armée européene" : double intox autour du 14-Juillet
france24fr.description: Le défilé du 14-Juillet 2026 à Paris "détourné" au profit de l’Union européenne et de l’Ukraine ? C’est ce qu’affirment plusieurs comptes prorusses sur les réseaux sociaux, évoquant un remplacement de La Marseillaise par l’hymne européen et la présence d’une "armée européenne". Le programme officiel ne prévoit cependant aucune modification de l’hymne ni du déroulé de la cérémonie.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 Live: Antonio Rüdiger über seine Rolle als »Social-Media-Buhmann«
spiegel.description: Antonio Rüdiger hatte seinen Auftritt bei der DFB-Pressekonferenz in Winston-Salem. Enttäuschung für Portugal und Cristiano Ronaldo. Und: Gleich startet England ins Turnier. Alles Wichtige im WM-Liveticker.

spiegel.title: Ukraine-Krieg: Von der Leyen will Aufnahme von Ukrainern in der EU einschränken
spiegel.description: Wegen Russlands Angriffskrieg fliehen zahlreiche Ukrainer in die EU. Kommissionspräsidentin von der Leyen will die Aufnahme nun limitieren. Das hat offenbar mit wehrfähigen Männern zu tun.

spiegel.title: Jeffrey Epstein: Das verraten seine Notizen aus dem Gefängnis
spiegel.description: Wie kam Jeffrey Epstein zu Tode? Eine Recherche der »New York Times« gibt Einblick in seine letzten Wochen. Sie zeigt einen Mann, der über Donald Trump schimpft und mit den Haftbedingungen hadert.

spiegel.title: Hamburg: Verfassungsschutz überprüft künftig sämtliche Bewerber für den Staatsdienst
spiegel.description: Hamburg schaut künftig genauer hin: Der Verfassungsschutz prüft alle Bewerber für den öffentlichen Dienst. Das beschloss der Senat. Nicht alle sind von dieser Idee begeistert.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: DR Kongo gegen Portugal: Kongo tanzt
spiegel.description: Erling Haaland und Kylian Mbappé trafen doppelt, Lionel Messi gar dreifach. Cristiano Ronaldo hingegen blieb beim Auftakt seiner Portugiesen blass. Kongo freut sich über das erste Tor seiner WM-Geschichte.

spiegel.title: Japan: Kartellbehörde ermittelt gegen Eis-Hersteller wegen Verdacht auf Absprachen
spiegel.description: Haben sechs japanische Eis-Hersteller illegale Preisabsprachen miteinander getroffen? Diesem Verdacht gehen Beamte der örtlichen Kartellbehörde nach. Fünf der Unternehmen bestätigten die Durchsuchung ihrer Büros.

spiegel.title: Peine: Verurteilter Mörder flieht auf Motorrad vor JVA-Mitarbeiter
spiegel.description: Bei einem begleiteten Freigang ging der Mann in eine Garage und brauste mit einem Motorrad davon: In Niedersachsen wird nach einem flüchtigen Mörder gefahndet.

spiegel.title: Revision in Berliner Vergewaltigungsfall: Wollte Marvin S. sein Opfer mit Drogen betäuben, um es zu vergewaltigen?
spiegel.description: Marvin S. gab einer 20-Jährigen Drogen und verging sich an der bewusstlosen Frau. Das Berliner Landgericht wertete dies als fahrlässige Körperverletzung und einfache Vergewaltigung. Jetzt muss der Fall neu verhandelt werden.

spiegel.title: Kevin Warsh: Neuer Fed-Chef tastet den US-Leitzins vorerst nicht an
spiegel.description: Erstmals ist der neue Fed-Chef Kevin Warsh bei der US-Notenbank für eine Zinsentscheidung verantwortlich. Forderungen von US-Präsident Donald Trump bleiben aber erstmal unerfüllt.

spiegel.title: Nationalsozialismus: »Die SS war der Motor für Hitlers Mordapparat«
spiegel.description: Von der Schlägertruppe zu den Organisatoren des Massenmords: Die SS galt als besonders brutale Gliederung im Gewaltsystem der Nazis. Historiker Jan Erik Schulte gibt Tipps, wie Angehörige möglicher Verbrecher weiterforschen können.

spiegel.title: Ölkrise: So geht es jetzt in der Straße von Hormus weiter
spiegel.description: Der Deal zwischen Amerikanern und Iranern weckt Hoffnungen auf ein Ende der Ölkrise. Noch aber ist das Abkommen wackelig und die Hormus-Meerenge vermint. Was das für die globale Wirtschaft bedeutet.

spiegel.title: BBC: Öffentlicher Rundfunk in Großbritannien baut 550 Jobs ab
spiegel.description: Der Sender BBC in Großbritannien muss sparen. Nun wurde der Abbau von 550 Stellen verkündet, sowohl in den Bereichen Nachrichten als auch Unterhaltung. Auch in der Führungsebene soll Personal eingespart werden.

spiegel.title: München: Juwelendiebe flüchten vor 40 Streifenwagen – Verdächtige festgenommen
spiegel.description: Ein Hubschrauber kreiste über München, Dutzende Streifenwagen fuhren durch die Straßen: Im Fall eines Juwelendiebstahls hat die Polizei zwei Verdächtige gestoppt.

spiegel.title: Viktor Orbán in Brüssel: Als eine Journalistin ihn mit »Herr Premierminister« anspricht, verzieht er keine Miene
spiegel.description: Der abgewählte Viktor Orbán trifft sich in Brüssel mit seinen rechten bis extrem rechten Freunden von den europäischen »Patrioten«. Der Ungar gibt sich kämpferisch. Nach seiner Zukunft gefragt, äußert er sich mehrdeutig.

spiegel.title: G7-Gipfel: »Ich bin der Chef« – wie Trump sich beim Treffen inszeniert
spiegel.description: Trump inszeniert sich beim G7-Treffen, Mikrofone zeichnen Small Talk über Melonis Wechsel unter die Nichtraucherinnen auf. Und: Dieses Mal gehen die Staats- und Regierungschefs geeint auseinander. Die Zusammenfassung im Video.

spiegel.title: Eva Maria Michelmann in Haft in Syrien: Das rätselhafte Verschwinden der Deutschen
spiegel.description: Monatelang fehlte jede Spur von Eva Maria Michelmann. Inzwischen ist klar: Die syrische Regierung hält die Deutsche in Damaskus fest. Ihre Angehörigen sagen, die Bundesregierung tue zu wenig, um sie freizubekommen.

spiegel.title: Antisemitismus in Deutschland: Rias-Bericht 2025 zeigt hohes Vorfallsniveau - wo bleibt der Aufschrei?
spiegel.description: Die Zahl der judenfeindlichen Vorfälle bleibt auf hohem Niveau, das zeigt der aktuelle Rias-Bericht. Das bittere Fazit: Antisemitismus ist inzwischen breitflächig in der Gesellschaft angekommen.

spiegel.title: Ostfriesland: Ex-Jugendtrainer soll Spieler geohrfeigt und belästigt haben
spiegel.description: In Ostfriesland läuft eine Anklage gegen einen ehemaligen Jugendfußballtrainer. Er soll Spieler geschlagen sowie gegen ihren Willen geküsst haben. Zur Tatzeit soll er selbst noch minderjährig gewesen sein.

observador.title: O dia em que a numerologia se perdeu num futebol de praia
observador.description: João Neves, o 1+5 da equipa, marcou aos 6' e deu o arranque ideal para 2026 ser como 1966 e 2006. Problema? Ficou-se por aí. Sim, Portugal teve muita bola – mas não soube o que fazer com ela (1-1).

observador.title: Incêndio em Castelo de Vide mobiliza sete meios aéreos
observador.description: Alerta foi dado às 17h24. Fogo tem uma frente ativa e consume uma área de mato, não havendo casas em risco. Quase 100 operacionais estão envolvidos no combate às chamas.

observador.title: Comentadores enganaram-se com o nome da RD Congo
observador.description: Foi um comentário passageiro, mas Darren Fletcher foi rápido a emendar o erro que acabara de cometer. Mas foi tarde demais e a internet já estava inundada de memes relativos ao seu lapso.

observador.title: Milão: maquinistas suspensos por espiar passageiras
observador.description: Imagens de mulheres foram capturadas pelas câmaras de vigilância dos transportes. Passageira reparou no telemóvel de motorista que viajava sentado à sua frente num elétrico e denunciou situação.

observador.title: Manteiga ou canário? O amarelo de Kate no arranque de Ascot
observador.description: Ao segundo dia do evento em Berkshire, a princesa de Gales resgata um look do armário e brincos de Isabel II. De Carlos III aos recém-casados, veja as imagens do clã real.

observador.title: IShowSpeed "converte" fãs de Messi no jogo de Portugal
observador.description: Entre selfies com adeptos, entrevistas improvisadas e debates sobre a eterna rivalidade entre Ronaldo e Messi, Speed chegou mesmo a oferecer uma camisola do CR7 a uma criança para a "converter".

observador.title: Mãe de Vozinha estará presente nos EUA
observador.description: Reencontro entre Vozinha e a mãe terá lugar em Miami no domingo, no jogo entre Cabo Verde e Uruguai. A história começou numa transmissão online e chegou a Marco Rubio, secretário de Estado dos EUA.

observador.title: Esclerose Múltipla: ULSM promete solução em semanas
observador.description: Doentes lançaram petição a exigir clínica dedicada, denunciando anos de espera e tratamentos em espaços não especializados. Administração tomou posse há mês e meio.

observador.title: Incêndio florestal em Spokane obriga 1.200 a abandonar casas
observador.description: Chamas deflagraram no estado de Washington e, impulsionadas por ventos fortes, atingiram Northwoods. Na manhã desta quarta, fogo estava apenas 10% dominado e já tinha consumido 91 hectares.

observador.title: Cinema Paris vai ser demolido para dar lugar a 19 habitações
observador.description: Inaugurado em 1931 na Rua Domingos Sequeira, na Estrela, o Cinema Paris encerrou em 1985. A votação dividiu o executivo entre direita e esquerda.

observador.title: Imagem de Diogo Jota foi exibida no Houston Stadium
observador.description: Foi sob o olhar atento dos seus pais que a imagem de Diogo Jota foi exibida no ecrãs do NRG Stadium durante o hino de Portugal, minutos antes das Quinas defrontarem a República Democrática do Congo.

observador.title: Luanda. UE financia projeto para modernizar gestão do lixo
observador.description: Luanda produz diariamente entre 6.000 e 8.000 toneladas de resíduos, enquanto a taxa de reciclagem continua inferior a 5%. Projeto tem como eixos centrais o reforço da governação e da regulação.

observador.title: Bispos portugueses afirmam que IA obriga Igreja a adaptar-se
observador.description: As conclusões das Jornadas Pastorais do Episcopado 2026 defendem literacia digital e ética tecnológica, alertando que evangelização não se mede por "gostos" ou "partilhas".

observador.title: OM e SPMS criam grupo de trabalho após falha no SNS
observador.description: Reunião decorreu esta quarta-feira. Ficaram ainda acordadas reuniões bimestrais e contacto direto em situações de falhas graves. Novo centro de dados em Évora previsto para o final do ano.

phys-org.title: Supernova origins explored through primordial black holes
phys-org.description: Dr. Shing-Chi Leung, assistant professor of physics at SUNY Polytechnic Institute, has published the article "Primordial Black Hole Triggered Type Ia Supernovae II: Comparison with Supernova Remnants and Galactic Chemical Evolution" in The Astrophysical Journal. phys-org.title: Single, childless workers fare worst at work-life balance
phys-org.description: New research from the University of St. Andrews is calling on employers to rethink flexible-working policies, warning that current approaches fail to reflect increasingly blurred boundaries between work and personal life.

phys-org.title: From 718 options to one standout, catalyst screening method reveals durable RuO₂ candidate
phys-org.description: Why settle for a trial-and-error approach, reviewing an almost endless number of combinations, when you can systematically narrow the list to something more manageable using established data and knowledge?

phys-org.title: Freshwater sediments may play a bigger role in slowing methane emissions than previously thought
phys-org.description: Methane is one of the most powerful greenhouse gases, and lakes and wetlands are among its largest natural sources. In many lakes, methane can be seen bubbling up from the bottom and escaping directly into the atmosphere.

phys-org.title: S-M-A-R-T! These researchers used math to crack Wordle
phys-org.description: Every day, millions of people play Wordle, the popular New York Times game that challenges users to guess a secret five-letter word. Using information theory, a team of researchers at Binghamton University, State University of New York, has developed a method to solve the game with a 99% success rate.

phys-org.title: LOFAR reveals spike-like repeating radio burst pairs in the solar corona
phys-org.description: The solar atmosphere is a turbulent and magnetized environment, with the release of magnetic energy readily manifesting as emission across the electromagnetic spectrum. Solar radio emission dominates the radio sky, with the brightest solar radio bursts generated via the plasma emission process. The emission has a complex frequency-time structure with many features that are yet to be understood.

phys-org.title: Climate advocacy by scientists shows mixed effects, no clear trust boost or backlash
phys-org.description: Scientists have become more visible in climate debates, engaging in public communication, policy advice, open letters, political demonstrations and even civil disobedience. Scientists who speak out on climate change have different effects depending on the context, according to research led by Lancaster University. phys-org.title: Dozens of active dust devils caught swirling across Mars canyon system
phys-org.description: The European Space Agency's Mars Express has captured part of Mars's Mamers Valles, a fascinating valley system speckled with brief, tornado-like whirlwinds known as dust devils.

phys-org.title: 'Alexa, tell me a joke': How talking to AI impacts young children's development
phys-org.description: Children are innately curious, and throughout any given day they come up with all manner of questions: Why don't fish have hair? Why do flowers wilt so quickly? Their need to understand the world—and develop their language skills and ideas—makes them tireless conversationalists.

phys-org.title: Fungi help lock carbon into Arctic fjord sediments
phys-org.description: Arctic fjords are among the most efficient natural systems for absorbing and storing carbon long term. However, as the Arctic is warming about four times faster than the global average, fjord ecosystems are changing rapidly. Against this backdrop, understanding the biological processes that regulate carbon storage is becoming increasingly important. Yet the microbial mechanisms that control whether carbon is stored in sediments or returned to the environment are still not fully understood.

phys-org.title: Swiss lake symbiosis reveals unexpected role in nitrogen cycling
phys-org.description: A publication led by researchers from the Max Planck Institute for Marine Microbiology in Bremen, Germany, shows that microscopic partnerships between ciliates and bacteria play a role in the nitrogen cycle of lakes. The study, published in The ISME Journal, investigates what determines the ecological niche of the remarkable symbiosis, and how strongly the host depends on its microbial partners.

phys-org.title: One of the world's most important climate threats has an image problem
phys-org.description: Deep in the Atlantic, a vast circulation of water carries heat from the tropics toward Greenland. This is the Atlantic meridional overturning circulation, or Amoc. It does this work largely out of sight, so it doesn't have the public profile of rainforests, polar ice caps or other huge climate-regulating systems.

phys-org.title: 'High-res' is the secret to finding alien life with the next great space telescope
phys-org.description: We're still in the definition phase of the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), but it seems like every week a new research group comes out with a paper helping to shape what is becoming one of the most important space telescopes of the 2040s. A new paper posted to the arXiv preprint server from a team of researchers led by Daniel Jaffe of the University of Texas at Austin contributes to this ongoing definition work by arguing that it's time HWO adopted a high-resolution near-IR spectro

phys-org.title: Bringing ancient light-sensing proteins back to life
phys-org.description: Resurrecting dinosaurs using DNA retrieved from a mosquito trapped in amber is a great movie plot, though it's less likely to happen in the real world. However, researchers have been trying to unlock the secrets behind the evolution of a single protein family to understand the evolution of ancestral proteins.

phys-org.title: AI could be trapped in a 'Carbon Valley' unless action is taken soon
phys-org.description: AI is growing fast, and keeping up means building more data centers, manufacturing advanced chips and powering the tech behind it. All of that comes with a carbon cost. AI advocates claim that in the long run, AI will save energy and cut carbon emissions across global industries.

phys-org.title: New swine influenza vaccination technique can greatly strengthen disease protection
phys-org.description: Husker scientists have developed a new swine influenza vaccination technique whose low cost and adaptability can greatly strengthen disease protection.

phys-org.title: Is the customer always right? Study finds rude customers hurt business
phys-org.description: Frontline employees who face rude or disrespectful customers are more likely to justify negative behaviors, from cutting corners to leaving their jobs, according to a new study.

phys-org.title: Reversible chirality switching in MoS₂ generates spin currents without magnets
phys-org.description: A newly developed method allows researchers to dynamically switch chirality—a particular lack of mirror symmetry—to generate spin currents in semiconductors, researchers from Science Tokyo report. Their approach relies on the reversible insertion and removal of small chiral molecules from the interlayer gaps of a layered, nonchiral semiconductor material using electrochemistry.

arxiv-ai.description:

arxiv-ai.description:

arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.17312v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models can arrive at the same answer through reasoning paths that are unstable, contradictory, or difficult to rank consistently -- a failure mode especially prevalent in multi-step deductive reasoning. Existing methods assess reliability primarily through output dispersion -- measuring how much sampled answers differ -- but this discards a complementary signal: whether the model can consistently rank competing reasoning candidates.

arxiv-ai.title: MemTrace: Probing What Final Accuracy Misses in Long-Term Memory
arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.17328v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents increasingly maintain long-term memory of user facts across sessions. Yet such memory is usually evaluated by aggregating accuracy over question rows or episodes. arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.17339v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speech offers a uniquely informative window into health by simultaneously engaging neurological, motor, respiratory, and vocal systems. Current clinical speech AI methods have largely progressed through isolated condition-specific studies, making results difficult to compare and generalization difficult to assess. arxiv-ai.title: Distributed General-Purpose Agent Networks: Architecture, Key Mechanisms, and Prototypes

arxiv-ai.title: Treatment Response Optimized Clinical Decision Support AI System via Digital Twin Simulation
arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.17405v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Clinical decision support AI systems (CDSASs) must adapt to evolving patient conditions in real-time while adhering to strict safety constraints. We present an online adaptive framework that integrates Treatment Effect (TE) estimation to quantify clinical benefits, a patient Digital Twin (DT) to simulate treatment trajectories, and Reinforcement Learning (RL) for sequential decision-making. arxiv-ai.title: Incumbent Advantage: Brand Bias and Cognitive Manipulation Dynamics in LLM Recommendation Systems
arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.17443v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are becoming a major way for consumers to find products, but we do not yet understand how brands compete in this new channel. We study brand dynamics in LLM recommendations using skincare products -- a category where consumers cannot easily judge quality before buying and must rely on brand reputation -- across three commercial LLMs (GPT-4o-mini, Claude Sonnet, Gemini 3 Flash), with a robustness check on search goods.

arxiv-ai.title: A Machine-Learned Comorbidity Index
arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.17450v1 Announce Type: new

arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.17453v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model agents are increasingly integrated into map services. Since map services are embedded in everyday-life scenarios rather than professional task settings, users often express their needs informally, resulting in underspecified queries with many unspoken needs, namely, implicit decision factors that are critical for user satisfaction. arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.17454v1 Announce Type: new

arXiv:2606.17507v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generative AI and large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to question generation and automated assessment. new-sci.title: Oldest known plague outbreak killed hunter-gatherer children
new-sci.description: DNA evidence shows that plague bacteria devastated a community in Siberia more than 5000 years ago, challenging the idea that there were no major disease outbreaks before the advent of farming and large settlements

new-sci.description: A study of 140,000 people suggests that a broadening of the diagnostic criteria for autism and ADHD explains the sharp rise in diagnoses, but that doesn't mean too many people are being told they are autistic or have ADHD

new-sci.title: Autism may have two distinct subtypes that vary by brain activity
new-sci.description: Evidence is mounting that there are distinct subtypes of autism, and now, scientists have found that the condition can vary according to the strength of people's brain connections

new-sci.title: The secrets to keeping your brain sharp in old age
new-sci.description: Neuroscientist Emily Rogalski studies superagers – people in their 80s or 90s with unusually keen memories, whose lifestyles suggest ways to slow cognitive decline

new-sci.title: A quantum state that lasts forever may finally be within our grasp
new-sci.description: Defying the laws of thermodynamics, experiments are beginning to show that a quantum state that is frozen forever might not be impossible. If we can tame it, it could unlock whole new types of matter

new-sci.title: Walking shark found in Papua New Guinea is new to science
new-sci.description: Hemiscyllium dudgeonae is the tenth recorded species of walking shark, which use their pectoral fins to move across reef flats, and its limited range means it may be at high risk of extinction

new-sci.title: Sperm have been made magnetic to allow IVF inside the body
new-sci.description: IVF could be done inside the body using a revolutionary technique that reduces the invasiveness of the traditional fertility treatment

new-sci.title: Arctic Ocean reaches tipping point that could be dire for marine life
new-sci.description: Disappearing sea ice is letting more sunlight in the Arctic Ocean and boosting phytoplankton growth, but this has depleted a crucial nutrient, which could severely affect animals higher up the food chain

new-sci.title: Technology is changing our perspective on nature – at every scale
new-sci.description: Inspired by Ariel Waldman’s docuseries Life Unearthed, columnist Annalee Newitz explores how microscopes, drones and specialised cameras are giving us an unprecedented view of nature from many different vantage points

new-sci.title: Has the answer to life's origins been hiding in our cells all along?
new-sci.description: The surprising discovery of mysterious blobs inside our cells is revolutionising our understanding of how life works, and how it got started

new-sci.title: The social media ban is an experiment – here’s how it will be studied
new-sci.description: Scientists have long grappled with how to measure the effect of social media on children. Now, the UK government has announced a total ban for everyone under 16, and researchers are rushing to design rigorous studies before it comes into effect

new-sci.title: Inside the start-up aiming for a giant leap in robot intelligence
new-sci.description: Physical Intelligence is drawing on the broad knowledge of large language models to help robots understand instructions and learn to carry out any task independently

new-sci.title: We may have finally solved cosmology's chicken-or-the-egg problem
new-sci.description: Galaxies and their supermassive black holes evolve together, but which came first is an ongoing question. Now we may finally have an answer, says columnist Leah Crane

new-sci.title: Are useful and error-free quantum computers only two years away?
new-sci.description: Quantum computing firm QuEra says it plans to make a fault-tolerant quantum computer and offer it to users through the cloud in 2028, which will require a real leap in engineering

new-sci.title: Why controversial ideas in science shouldn't always be dismissed
new-sci.description: Researchers suggesting that the keto diet could treat mental health conditions find themselves uncomfortably aligned with people like vaccine-sceptic Robert F. Kennedy Jr, but that is not a reason to reject the idea

new-sci.title: What is a ‘normal’ memory slowdown, and when should I worry?
new-sci.description: Lapses in memory are a normal part of ageing but can also be signs of dementia. Here’s how to distinguish between typical brain ageing and cognitive decline

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

proj-syn.title: Learning from the Right Sovereign Wealth Funds
proj-syn.description: The Gulf has made establishing a sovereign wealth fund seem like a strategic—and glamorous—choice, leading countries like Canada to launch their own. But Latin America has run this experiment many times over the years, offering a more realistic view of an SWF’s pitfalls and promise.

proj-syn.title: Europe Cannot Afford Another Lost Year
proj-syn.description: European businesses need simpler rules, faster permitting, affordable energy, stronger infrastructure, and a fully functioning single market. The longer that European policymakers fail to deliver on these policies, the greater Europe’s competitiveness challenge will become.

proj-syn.title: White House Fight Night
proj-syn.description: The venue on the South Lawn for UFC Freedom 250 was built, approved, lit, filmed, defended, watched, and enjoyed as part of a celebration of freedom. President Donald Trump’s chosen object to represent that celebration was a cage.

proj-syn.title: The US-Iran Agreement Is a First Step
proj-syn.description: While the recently announced US-Iranian memorandum of understanding is certainly good news, it is not definitive. The path from a statement of diplomatic intent to a fully restored, non-inflationary energy supply chain is fraught with political, technical, and physical risks.

proj-syn.title: Developing-Country Risk Is Being Mispriced
proj-syn.description: When investors say there are no “bankable” projects in developing economies, they are typically referring less to project quality than to the cost of capital. But the assumptions driving up risk premia are not supported by the evidence, and until this changes, the misallocation of capital will continue to undermine development.

proj-syn.title: The Fed Has Been Honest and Stupid
proj-syn.description: It would be easy—and a mistake—to blame the US Federal Reserve’s many blunders on corrupt bureaucrats or imagined conspiracies. The truth of the matter is that the central bank relies on an outdated regional map and lagging indicators that no longer tell the whole story, while battling macroeconomic blazes that politicians stoke.

proj-syn.title: A New Framework for Climate Displacement
proj-syn.description: Global warming is already uprooting communities and impoverishing people who remain in vulnerable areas—a crisis that is often overshadowed by the focus on decarbonization. But the Global Climate Mobility Principles offer policymakers a framework for ensuring that these individuals maintain their agency and rights.

proj-syn.title: Peace With Iran Is All About Lebanon Now
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump says that he "calls the shots" on negotiating with Iran, and Israel has no choice but to submit to a deal that undermines its security interests. But a deal that makes Trump the protector of Lebanon—and, by extension, Iran-backed Hezbollah—could put the US and Israel on a collision course.

proj-syn.title: Every British Prime Minister’s Nightmare
proj-syn.description: The true nature of Britain’s “special relationship” with the United States has far more to do with American financiers’ willingness to keep borrowing to purchase British government debt than with history, culture, or Britain’s defense needs. Every UK Prime Minister must bear this burden, which is rapidly becoming unsustainable.

proj-syn.title: India’s Unfinished Reform Agenda
proj-syn.description: Elevated oil prices, potentially strong El Niño conditions during the monsoon season, and the tariff-induced fragmentation of global trade are bearing down on the Indian economy and will likely be a drag on GDP growth. But these adverse conditions may be a blessing in disguise if they force India to complete its economic reform agenda.

proj-syn.title: The Middle East’s New Normal
proj-syn.description: The most likely outcome of the Iran war is not peace but an unsatisfying ceasefire that leaves the underlying issues unresolved. This will mean an uneasy equilibrium in which Gulf countries go their own way, US influence wanes, and the regional order remains unsettled.

proj-syn.title: No Bridge Over Healing Waters for the G7
proj-syn.description: The French G7 presidency’s focus on global imbalances is both welcome and problematic. While long-standing trade imbalances between the United States, Europe, and China are, if anything, becoming even more troublesome, the leaders’ summit in Évian-les-Bains will do nothing to address the problem.

proj-syn.title: Are Government Stakes the Key to AI Sovereignty?
proj-syn.description: At first glance, reports that the US and Chinese governments are both considering taking stakes in national AI champions would seem to suggest a convergence between the world’s two leading AI powers. But a closer look reveals stark differences in their underlying strategies.

proj-syn.title: From the American Revolution to Universal Suffrage
proj-syn.description: Britain’s attempt to crush the American Revolution exposed a constitutional crisis at the heart of its empire. One English statesman saw in it proof that only broader suffrage could check royal power, tame corruption, and ensure that imperial rule remained compatible with liberty.

proj-syn.title: Jefferson’s Revolutionary Language
proj-syn.description: Of the delegates who assembled in Philadelphia in 1776 for the Second Continental Congress, only Thomas Jefferson possessed the skill, knowledge, and linguistic gifts to make the Declaration of Independence an immortal text. He was the self-appointed conscience of America, and sensational imagery was his stock-in-trade.

proj-syn.title: The Declaration of the Enslaved
proj-syn.description: For African-Americans, the Declaration of Independence was nothing but a “thin veil to cover the crimes” of slavery, as Frederick Douglass put it. Inspired by Haiti’s Declaration of Independence, free and enslaved Black people in the US found themselves subverting America’s founding document to achieve their own emancipation.

proj-syn.title: Free-Market Capitalism Is Destroying US Democracy
proj-syn.description: Far from two sides of the same coin, free-market capitalism and democracy are fundamentally incompatible. The only way to restore US democracy is to transform the system, so that it compensates innovators but limits their market power, while ensuring that the benefits of economic progress are more equitably shared.
